subject: MAP kickoff: success criteria, exit gates, and acceptance test runway
messages:
From: Emma Jordan <emma.jordan@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@bluepeakhealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff: evaluation success criteria & timeline

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the intro last week. BluePeak's evaluation team is ready to start a short POC to validate inference reliability and safety for our clinical-assist workflows. Before we spin up infrastructure, procurement and engineering asked that we align on a mutual action plan (MAP) that defines: success criteria, exit gates, and concrete acceptance tests.

High-level constraints from our side:
- Evaluation window: target completion by Jan 28 (we have an exec review on Jan 29)
- Security: SOC2 evidence required in parallel (we’ve attached our evaluation context)
- Quality: we will run a labeled 500-case test set and expect no more than 2 critical errors and overall concordance above 92% (more details in the doc)

Can you put together a short MAP with owners and the acceptance tests (smoke, regression, perf, and security evidence) so we can share with procurement? Also include a realistic timeline and any support you’ll need from our side.

Attachment: BluePeak-Eval-Context.pdf (summary, test-set spec)

—Emma
Emma Jordan
Director, Clinical Innovation
BluePeak Health

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: evaluation success criteria & timeline

Emma — thanks, this is helpful context. I’ve drafted a compact MAP below that focuses on measurable acceptance tests and clear owners so procurement can sign off quickly. The plan assumes a hosted Dedicated evaluation environment with a reserved GPU pool for the 2-week window.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for BluePeak clinical-assist flows with measurable safety, latency, and throughput targets so BluePeak can proceed to a pilot.

- Success criteria (pass conditions):
  1) Safety: <=2 critical failures on BluePeak 500-case labeled set; no high-severity hallucinations for clinical prompt templates.
  2) Quality: overall concordance >= 92% on labeled set; per-class precision > 90% for triage prompts.
  3) Performance: 99th percentile token latency < 250ms for 512-token typical requests under a 5rps sustained load.
  4) Reliability: 99.9% availability during the evaluation window.
  5) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence folder shared; network isolation and KMS integration validated.

- Exit gates (fail/pass decisions):
  • Gate A — Smoke & Setup (Day 1–2): environment provisioned, sample inference run, access granted to BluePeak. Owner: Marissa (CS).
  • Gate B — Safety & Quality (Day 3–10): run labeled 500-case test, measure concordance and critical failures. Owner: BluePeak test lead (Emma) + Karthik (perf & eval).
  • Gate C — Perf & Scale (Day 8–12): load tests to verify p99 latency and autoscale behavior. Owner: Karthik.
  • Gate D — Procurement & Signoff (Day 12–14): SOC2 artifacts, cost estimate, contract signoff. Owner: Lauren (bizops).

- Acceptance tests (concrete):
  1) Labeled test run: run BluePeak 500-case set via reproducible harness; store outputs to shared Drive and run concordance/issue classifier.
  2) Regression suite: 200 edge-case prompts (safety-focused) with pass/fail rules; must have 0 critical regressions.
  3) Perf suite: 1k-request load test with 5rps sustained and bursts to 20rps; verify p50/p95/p99 latencies and memory/KV cache behavior.
  4) End-to-end smoke: API auth, function-calling pipeline, and binary attachment handling (if used).
  5) Security checklist: SOC2 artifact handover, KMS key exchange test, audit log sample review.

- Measurements & artifacts: shared Drive folder with run logs, aggregated metrics (latency histograms), labeled-case diff report, and incident log.

- Support needed from BluePeak: test set access, whitelisted IPs for VPC peering (if needed), and procurement contact for contract review.

Next steps: I’ll convert this into a short MAP doc and share a one-page timeline. Can the BluePeak team confirm owners for Gate B and the labeled test owner? Also cc’ing Marissa, Karthik, and Lauren to confirm internal owners and resource availability.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Vivek — this looks good and granular, thank you. A couple of clarifications from procurement and engineering:

1) Timeline: Jan 28 completion is firm. Any items that could push critical Gate D past Jan 28 will require a brief written exception.
2) Quality threshold: the 92% concordance is our target; however procurement flagged the commercial trigger: if concordance <89% we will stop and revisit scope.
3) Security: procurement needs a checklist and a copy of your SOC2 report; Samir will own the security handoff.
4) Contract: procurement prefers a short-term committed Dedicated SKU for the trial (30 days) — can you send an indicative cost and a DocuSign link?

Attachment: BluePeak-procurement-terms.docx

Emma

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: evaluation success criteria & timeline

Emma / Team — quick follow-up with the acceptance-test plan and owners (concrete runbook). I’m leaving notes so we can operationalize each gate.

Acceptance test runbook (owners & pass criteria):
- Gate A (Smoke & Setup) — Day 1–2
Owner: Marissa (CS)
Steps: provision Dedicated pool, validate API keys, run 10-sample smoke set.
Pass: 10/10 smoke samples complete, access confirmed.

- Gate B (Safety & Quality) — Day 3–10
Owner: BluePeak test lead (Emma) + Karthik (eval run)
Steps: run 500-case labeled set using the provided harness; generate diff report; flag any critical failures.
Pass: concordance >= 92% AND <=2 critical failures. If concordance is between 89–92%, trigger a remediation sprint (2 days) and re-run. If <89% -> fail the MAP and pause procurement.

- Gate C (Perf & Scale) — Day 8–12
Owner: Karthik
Steps: run 1k-request load test (5rps baseline, burst to 20rps), track p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory/KV metrics.
Pass: p99 < 250ms for 512-token typical requests; 5rps sustained with no failures.

- Gate D (Procurement & Signoff) — Day 12–14
Owner: Lauren
Steps: share SOC2 artifacts, cost summary, and DocuSign; procurement completes PO.
Pass: signed SOW/PO or documented exception.

Rollback & fallback triggers:
- Safety rollback: any critical hallucination that leads to clinical risk -> immediate suspension and conference call within 2 hours.
- Perf rollback: sustained error rate >1% during perf run -> pause and isolate workload.

Owners recap: Karthik (perf/tests), Marissa (onboarding/ops), Lauren (contract/procurement), Vivek (exec escalation).

We’ll prepare automated scripts to produce the concordance report and the perf histograms. I’ll attach the scripts and create a shared Drive folder.

On the commercial ask: Vivek, Lauren — BluePeak requested a 30-day committed Dedicated SKU for the test. I’ll scope resource needs once procurement gives us the PO window.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Timeline: Gate A (Jan 22), Gate B run (Jan 23–26), Gate C perf (Jan 25–27), Gate D signoff (Jan 28).
- Commercial: Indicative cost and DocuSign link sent to procurement separately; Lauren to own contract cadence.

- BluePeak: provide whitelisted IPs and the labeled dataset access by EOD Jan 21.
- Redwood: Marissa to provision Dedicated SKU; Karthik to prepare perf harness; Lauren to send DocuSign.

If there are no objections, I’ll schedule the kickoff now.
